assessment: This work contributes interesting data to both the circadian and sleep fields as it presents evidence that clock gene expression in peripheral tissues can be regulated in sleep-wake-state- and peripheral-circadian-dependent manners. To support this idea, the authors monitor sleep-wake state, as well as PER2 expression (utilizing a PER2-luciferase system), in both intact or SCN-lesioned freely behaving mice. Analysis of central and peripheral PER2LUC levels, under diverse sleep protocols, and aided by mathematical models allows them to support the idea that in peripheral tissues the clock gene circuitry integrates sleep-wake information, potentially contributing to behavioral adaptability to homeostatically respond to different challenges.
